messages.author: 43be103b90cd24bb
messages.subject: Factor scores in using lavPredict()
parts:
Hi there! 

I hope you can help - I'm trying to create factor scores to be used in linear regression analyses. 

I conducted an CFA using items from two Likert scale questionnaires and derived four factors (using the lavaan function cfa()).

I would now like to see how these factors relate to other variables in regression analyses. Therefore, I would like to create factor scores to be used in my regression analyses. At the moment the code I have to create the factor scores is:

factor_scores <- lavPredict(
  object = cfa.model, 
  newdata = dat, 
  method = "EBM", # "EBM" Empirical Bayes Model or "ML" maximum likelihood are suggested for ordinal data
  label = TRUE
  )

This all runs fine and gives me factor scores - my first question is - what do these factor scores represent and how would I interpret these factor scores in the linear regression analysis (factor_score1 ~ variable1 +variable2)? 

I can see that you can specify in the function what type you would like ( "lv", "ov", "ythat" and "fy"). I didn't really understand the difference between these, could you please explain what these different types represent using examples? 

I was thinking that it makes sense to create probabilities (using type "fy") so that in my regression, I can say for example: variable1 was significantly associated with estimate coefficient lower probability of reporting factor1. But I'm worried that I'm not interpreting this correctly!

Secondly, I tried to run the same code and added type = "fy", but this produced the error: 
Error in lav_predict_fy_internal(X = data.obs[[g]], yhat = YHAT[[g]],  : 
  lavaan ERROR: link must be probit or logit

Could you please suggest how to derive probability factor scores using LavPredict() when your factors are derived through several Likert scale items? 

A colleague of mine suggested adapting the factor score so that it reflects the same levels as the items it was formed on - could this also be a possibility? So, each item within a factor is based on a response from 0-3, could we create a factor score that was also on a scale of 0-3? 

I look forward to hearing your thoughts and suggestions - many thanks in advance!
Katie

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Factor scores in using lavPredict()
parts:
Katie

If you are looking at the relation of the factors with other variables, the best way is to include those variables in a latent regression in lavaan. Any particular reason you "need" to do this out of lavaan with factor scores?

The factor scores are in the metric of the factors in your cfa() model. So depending on how you set their metric and direction of the items is how you interpret them

You can have them in the scale of the indicators if you set the factor scale with effect coding method ofidentification

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Factor scores in using lavPredict()
parts: Could you share the arguments to have the factor scores in the scale of the indicators?

You can't.  Marker-variable and effects-coding methods do not transfer the observed-scale units to the latent variable, unless error variances are zero.  The common factor doesn't have a scale because we haven't directly measured it, and it is only a component of the observed indicators.

https://psycnet.apa.org/doi/10.1037/1082-989X.7.2.210
How can I set the factor scale with 'effect coding method of identification'?

See the effect.coding= argument's description in the ?lavOptions help page.
